title: Boss: harden the account service
summary: A security ticket: validate tenant slugs properly, pull real error lines out of a log, redact a codename and lint a .env file.

steps.title: Ticket SEC-221
body: > **SEC-221: input handling in the account service.** Found in the penetration test. Assigned to you.
1. Tenant slugs were accepted with spaces, semicolons and trailing newlines. Write the check properly.
2. The incident timeline needs the real `ERROR` lines from the log, not every line that mentions one.
3. The release notes must not mention the internal codename. Redact it as a whole word.
4. The deploy tool chokes on malformed `.env` files. Report the bad lines by number.
Every part is about **where** a match may start and end.

steps.title: Tenant slugs
prompt: The service accepts a slug when `Regex.IsMatch(slug, pattern)` is true, and these checks run the same way. A valid
slug:
- is 3 to 32 characters of lowercase ASCII letters, digits and `-`,
- starts with a letter,
- does not end with `-`.
Nothing else may get through, not even a trailing newline.
steps.explain: First character, middle `{1,30}`, last character: 3 to 32 in total. `\A` and `\z` make `IsMatch` check the whole slug; `$` would let the newline through.

steps.title: The real error lines
prompt: The whole log is one string. Find every line that **starts** with a timestamp `HH:MM:SS`, a space and the word
`ERROR`, and match the entire line. Indented lines from stack dumps, `ERRORS` and timestamps quoted inside a
message do not count.

input: 09:12:03 ERROR indented, from a stack dump

steps.explain: Multiline makes `^` match at each line start, `\b` refuses `ERRORS`, and `.*` stops at the end of the line.

steps.title: Redact the codename
prompt: Write `string RedactCodename(string text, string codename)` that replaces every whole-word occurrence of
`codename`, in any case, with `***`. Parts of longer words stay. The codename comes from config, so escape it.
`RedactCodename("Falcon ships Friday; falconry is unaffected; FALCON.", "falcon")` returns
`"*** ships Friday; falconry is unaffected; ***."`. `System.Text.RegularExpressions` is already imported.
template: Dojo.Eq("whole words in any case", "*** ships Friday; falconry is unaffected; ***.", RedactCodename("Falcon ships Friday; falconry is unaffected; FALCON.", "falcon"));
Dojo.Eq("_ joins words, - does not", "Project Falcon_v2 and ***-v2", RedactCodename("Project Falcon_v2 and falcon-v2", "falcon"));
Dojo.Eq("a dot in the codename is literal", "see *** not v1x2", RedactCodename("see v1.2 not v1x2", "v1.2"));
Dojo.Eq("no codename, no change", "nothing here", RedactCodename("nothing here", "falcon"));

steps.title: Lint the .env file
prompt: Write `List<int> BadLines(string env)` that returns the line numbers (counting from 1) of the malformed lines in
a `.env` file, in order. Lines are separated by `\n`; a line may end in `\r` (Windows), which you should ignore.
- A **blank** line (empty, or only spaces and tabs) is fine.
- A **comment** (first non-blank character `#`) is fine.
- Every other line must start with a key and `=`: the key is an uppercase ASCII letter followed by uppercase
letters, digits or `_`. The value after `=` may be anything, even empty.
```text
API_KEY=abc          fine
api_key=abc          bad: lowercase key
API KEY=x            bad: space in the key
=x                   bad: no key
PORT                 bad: no =
Check each line on its own with `\A` anchors. `System.Text.RegularExpressions` is already imported.
template: Dojo.Eq("lines 4, 5, 8, 9 and 10 are bad", new List<int> { 4, 5, 8, 9, 10 }, BadLines(dojoEnv));
Dojo.Eq("Windows line endings", new List<int> { 2 }, BadLines("A=1\r\nbad line\r\n"));

Dojo.Eq("a clean file has no bad lines", new List<int>(), BadLines("# ok
A=1
B_2=x=y
"));
Dojo.Eq("an empty file has no bad lines", new List<int>(), BadLines(""));
